observations.text: Users explicitly ask for stronger research skills, specialized depth, verified sources, and proven workflows.
A separate skill-quality thread calls for repeatability, schemas, objective evaluation, and benchmarks rather than generic expertise personas.
One reported custom Codex research system works well, showing the job can be solved without this particular packaged skill.

inferences.text: The defensible product wedge is auditability and community-evidence integrity, implemented as a testable procedure rather than generic deep-research prose.

recommendation.text: Build and publish a portable, local-first skill with deterministic provenance, independence, WTP, counterevidence, and coverage gates, then evaluate it against a no-skill baseline.
caveats: This quick purposive study supports a prototype decision, not a market-size or population-demand claim.
The research-quality signal is recurring inside this sample; the procedural-skill signal remains anecdotal because every supporting record comes from one thread.
Neither signal establishes willingness to pay.

next_tests: Run preregistered cold baseline-versus-skill trials on frozen adversarial community datasets.
Repeat the demand study on GitHub Issues or Discussions and Hacker News to test source diversity.
coverage_notes: All four Reddit searches were manually inspected; two result sets were truncated after one page.
Engagement snapshots are retained for context and excluded from scoring.
stop_reason: The quick-mode source, thread, community, platform, and counterquery floors were reached; further work is assigned to the preregistered cold evaluation and cross-platform follow-up.
